metadata.title: Why the Server Hands Back an Encrypted Context You're Only Going to Echo
metadata.purpose: Take compaction apart in the Teardown register: two payloads, two jobs. Explain why the server hands back both a readable summary and an encrypted blob, judge the design choice, and land the carry-out that the readable summary is for your eyes while the encrypted blob is what actually carries the conversation's memory forward.
metadata.anchor_pair: B02 -> B04 (twenty-turn compaction case, paid off with the blob passed forward instead of a message replay)

beats.narration_text: The obvious read: the summary Claude hands back after compaction is what it remembers, because it's the part you can actually read. Wrong — that summary is for your eyes, not for the model. So why does the server hand back an encrypted blob you're only going to echo?

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'The summary is what Claude remembers, right?', hesitates on 'remembers', corrects to 'shows you', lands the real question

props.text:

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md WRITER LAW. TIMING LAW: 20-35 word narration + lead_silence_s 0.8 to give the typing a >=9s window; verify media/B00.mp4 >= 8s and that the correction ('remembers' -> 'shows you') is visible on a late frame.

beats.narration_text: Here's what's actually happening. A conversation gets long enough, compaction fires, and the API hands back two payloads side by side: a readable summary, and an opaque encrypted blob. Every instinct points at the readable one — you can see it, so surely that's what Claude sees on the next call. Pass only that into the next call, and the context breaks anyway. They optimized for two different jobs at once: an artifact you can debug with your eyes, and a memory artifact the server can rebuild. Two payloads, because one object can't cleanly do both.

shot.new_visual_element: A tall message stack branching into two outputs; the readable-summary path dead-ends

production_viz.label: Two outputs, one dead end
production_viz.mechanic: A tall stack of message bubbles labelled 'LONG CHAT' on cream. It branches into two paths: 'READABLE SUMMARY' (thin, ink only) heading toward 'NEXT CALL' but stopping short with a break mark; 'ENCRYPTED BLOB' (solid card, terracotta border) continuing unbroken toward 'NEXT CALL'.

beats.narration_text: Concrete case. A twenty-turn conversation crosses the threshold, and compaction fires. What comes back is two fields, side by side. content reads "Earlier conversation summarized" in plain English, right next to encrypted_content — a sealed string starting "EpwBCioIDxgC…". Thread the readable text into the next call and the context collapses. Thread the blob back and the model picks up where it left off. Same message, two payloads: one you can read, one the server can rebuild.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR - the stack collapsing into an open speech bubble and a sealed box; only the box's path continues

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR - collapse into two outputs, one path holds
production_viz.mechanic: THE ANCHOR. A tall stack of twenty message bubbles collapses into one block, which emits two shapes: an open speech bubble labelled 'content: "Earlier conversation summarized"' and a sealed box labelled 'encrypted_content: "EpwBCioIDxgC..."' with a terracotta border. An arrow from the speech bubble toward 'NEXT CALL' breaks with an X; the arrow from the sealed box reaches 'NEXT CALL' intact. THIS COLLAPSE COMPOSITION RETURNS AT B04.

beats.narration_text: Here's why the mechanism works this way. The readable text is display and debug — a courtesy for humans and logs, not a message the model consumes. The encrypted blob is a different object: a server-verifiable token, signed by the API so it knows it produced it. Feed it back and the server unpacks turn boundaries, roles, metadata — the full structured context. A plain-English summary throws all of that away the moment it flattens twenty turns into a paragraph.

shot.new_visual_element: Speech bubble labelled 'display only'; sealed box unpacking into turn boundaries / roles / metadata

production_viz.label: Display text vs. server-verifiable token
production_viz.mechanic: Left: the open speech bubble from B02, labelled underneath 'DISPLAY / DEBUG ONLY' in ink. Right: the sealed box, terracotta border, unpacking (arrows fanning out) into three labelled fields: 'turn boundaries', 'roles', 'metadata'. Beneath the speech bubble, the same three field labels appear crossed out in ink, captioned 'thrown away'.

beats.narration_text: Back to the twenty-turn case. On the next call you send the blob, not the transcript. The server doesn't replay twenty messages — it rebuilds the compressed context straight from the token, in one step. That's the design trade-off exposed: they split the work into a memory object the server owns and a display object you own. The summary isn't dead weight — it's still exactly what you'd show a user, log to a file, or hand to a monitoring tool. Two jobs, two payloads. Send the wrong one to the next call and only one of those jobs fails.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS - 20 messages crossed out, replaced by one token; the speech bubble persists, labelled still useful

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS - one token, not a replay
production_viz.mechanic: THE B02 COLLAPSE COMPOSITION RETURNS: the twenty-message stack now shown crossed out in ink beside a single sealed box (terracotta border) with an unbroken arrow to 'NEXT CALL'. Off to the side, the open speech bubble from B02/B03 persists, unbroken, captioned 'still useful — for display' in ink (no accent — it is not the thing that failed).

beats.narration_text: The readable summary is for your eyes; the encrypted blob is what actually carries the conversation's memory forward.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's a prompt you can paste into Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini. You're building a multi-turn PHP app on the Anthropic SDK. Show me how to detect a compaction block in the response, then write the code that threads the encrypted_content blob — not the human-readable summary — back into the next messages array. Explain what breaks if you send the summary text instead. Go deeper: what should happen when the API key rotates mid-session, or the compaction event arrives while a response is still streaming? Liam, in for Bear.
